questions.explanation: Problem identification includes trend analysis and detection of recurring or duplicate issues.

questions.prompt: Which activity is part of problem control?
choices: Trend analysis of historic incident records
Reassessing the status of unresolved known errors
Problem analysis and documenting workarounds and known errors
Logging and categorizing new user incidents
questions.explanation: Problem control focuses on analysis and documenting workarounds and known errors.

questions.prompt: Which activity is part of error control?
choices: Identifying potential permanent solutions, which may result in a change request
Detecting duplicate and recurring issues among incident records
Logging and prioritizing new incidents reported by users
Agreeing service level targets with customers
questions.explanation: Error control manages known errors, including identifying permanent fixes and reviewing workarounds.

questions.prompt: How should problems be prioritized for analysis in problem control?
choices: According to which team reported the related incidents
Based on the risk they pose, considering impact and probability
In the order the problems were identified
According to how many staff are available to investigate
questions.explanation: Problems are prioritized according to risk so effort is focused where it matters most.

questions.prompt: Why is a workaround documented in a problem record?
choices: So the service desk no longer needs to be involved
Because a workaround removes the need for any resolution
So the problem record can be closed straight away
So it can be reused for related incidents and reviewed and improved over time
questions.explanation: Documented workarounds speed incident resolution and are reassessed during error control.

questions.prompt: A known error has a workaround, and a permanent fix is too costly compared with its impact. What may be appropriate?
choices: Raise an emergency change to apply the costly fix immediately
Close all related incidents and the problem without further action
Continue using the workaround and keep the known error under review
Delete the known error record since no fix is planned
questions.explanation: When a permanent fix is not justified, an effective workaround may be retained while the known error is periodically reassessed.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most closely involved when problem management identifies a permanent solution that requires modifying a live system?
choices: Service request management
Relationship management
Change enablement
Supplier management
questions.explanation: Permanent fixes are usually implemented through a change request handled by change enablement.

questions.prompt: How do incident management and problem management differ?
choices: Incident management restores service quickly, while problem management investigates and manages underlying causes
They are the same practice described under two different names
Problem management deals with hardware, incident management with software
Incident management finds root causes, while problem management restores service
questions.explanation: The two practices are closely linked but have different objectives and timescales.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the service request management practice?
choices: To capture demand for incident resolution and service requests, and act as the entry point and single point of contact for the service provider with all its users
To set clear business-based targets for service levels and ensure delivery of services is properly assessed, monitored and managed against these targets
To minimize the negative impact of incidents by restoring normal service operation as quickly as possible
To support the agreed quality of a service by handling all predefined, user-initiated service requests in an effective and user-friendly manner
questions.explanation: Service request management handles the normal, expected requests that are part of service delivery.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a typical service request?
choices: A request for access to a shared folder
A report that the email system is down
A high-risk upgrade to a core system
An investigation into recurring network failures
questions.explanation: Requests for access, information, resources or service actions are service requests; outages are incidents.

questions.prompt: How should service requests be handled wherever possible?
choices: Only by senior engineers
With a fresh assessment by a change board each time
Only through walk-in support
Using standardized and automated workflows
questions.explanation: Because requests are predefined, they can be standardized and automated to improve efficiency.

questions.prompt: Which statement about service requests and approvals is correct?
choices: Approvals for service requests are always handled by suppliers
Every service request must be approved by the sponsor before fulfilment
Policies should define which requests can be fulfilled with limited or no additional approvals
Service requests are pre-defined, so approvals are never needed
questions.explanation: Clear policies streamline fulfilment while maintaining appropriate control.

questions.prompt: A user submits a compliment about excellent support received. How might this be handled?
choices: As an incident with low priority
As a problem for later analysis
As a normal change to the service
As a type of service request covering feedback, compliments and complaints
questions.explanation: Feedback, compliments and complaints can be handled within service request management.

questions.prompt: A user asks for information on how to configure a printer. Which practice should handle this?
choices: Deployment management
Problem management
Service request management
Change enablement
questions.explanation: A request for information is a typical service request.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the service desk practice?
choices: To support the agreed quality of a service by handling all predefined, user-initiated service requests in an effective and user-friendly manner
To minimize the negative impact of incidents by restoring normal service operation as quickly as possible
To establish and nurture the links between the organization and its stakeholders at strategic and tactical levels
To capture demand for incident resolution and service requests, and act as the entry point and single point of contact for the service provider with all its users
questions.explanation: The service desk is the user-facing point of contact for incidents and requests.

questions.prompt: Which skills does ITIL 4 emphasize most for service desk staff?
choices: Deep specialist expertise in every technology
Software development
Empathy and effective communication with users
Contract negotiation
questions.explanation: The service desk focuses on understanding users and the business context, not necessarily deep technical skill.

questions.prompt: Which statement about service desk channels is correct?
choices: Users should be encouraged to attend in person for faster resolution
Telephone should be the only channel so that requests can be tracked
Service desks may use phone, email, chat, service portals, walk-in and social media channels
Email and chat should be avoided because they cannot be prioritized
questions.explanation: Modern service desks provide multiple channels to suit users' needs.

questions.prompt: Staff in several countries and time zones work together as one service desk using shared tools. What is this arrangement called?
choices: A change advisory board
A virtual service desk
A walk-in service desk
A swarming team
questions.explanation: A virtual service desk lets geographically dispersed staff operate as a single team.

questions.prompt: Which tool supports the service desk in resolving issues quickly at first contact?
choices: A change schedule
A continual improvement register
A supplier contract database
A knowledge base
questions.explanation: Knowledge bases help staff find solutions and workarounds quickly.

questions.prompt: What does ITIL 4 say about the service desk's understanding of the organization?
choices: The service desk should focus on closing tickets rather than business context
The service desk mainly needs deep technical knowledge of the infrastructure
Business knowledge is the concern of relationship managers, not the service desk
The service desk should understand the wider organization, business processes and users
questions.explanation: Understanding the business context helps the service desk support users and prioritize effectively.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the service level management practice?
choices: To align the organization's practices and services with changing business needs through ongoing improvement
To establish and nurture the links between the organization and its stakeholders at strategic and tactical levels
To ensure that the organization's suppliers and their performance are managed appropriately to support the seamless provision of quality products and services
To set clear business-based targets for service levels and ensure delivery of services is properly assessed, monitored and managed against these targets
questions.explanation: Service level management defines and tracks service performance against business-based targets.

questions.prompt: What is a service level agreement (SLA)?
choices: A description of a known error together with its documented workaround
A record of all changes that have been authorized for the coming month
A contract between a service provider and its hardware supplier covering delivery times
A documented agreement between a service provider and a customer that identifies both services required and the expected level of service
questions.explanation: SLAs capture agreed services and service levels between provider and customer.

questions.prompt: A provider's SLA reports show all targets met, yet customers complain about poor service. What is this situation often called?
choices: The watermelon SLA effect
Shift-left
Error control
Swarming
questions.explanation: Like a watermelon, reports look green outside while customers experience red inside, often because metrics are too narrow.

questions.prompt: Which characteristic makes an SLA more effective?
choices: It includes outcome-based metrics that reflect the customer's experience
It focuses on technical metrics such as server uptime
It uses detailed technical language for precision
It is written by the provider without customer involvement
questions.explanation: SLAs should be related to defined services, simply written and include metrics that reflect business outcomes.

questions.prompt: Which activity helps service level management understand what customers value?
choices: Running deployment pipelines for new releases
Analysing configuration item records and their relationships
Reviewing supplier invoices against contract terms
Customer engagement, such as listening and asking about their business needs
questions.explanation: Engaging with customers to understand their needs is key to setting meaningful service levels.

questions.prompt: Which source of information is used by service level management?
choices: The change schedule and the record of authorized changes
Configuration records held in the configuration management system
Customer feedback, operational metrics and business metrics
Supplier contracts and their associated penalty clauses
questions.explanation: A combination of feedback and metrics gives a complete picture of service performance.

questions.prompt: Which skills are most relevant for service level management?
choices: Software coding and automated testing
Network cabling and hardware repair
Accounting and payroll administration
Relationship management, business liaison and business analysis
questions.explanation: Service level management relies on understanding customers and translating needs into targets.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the information security management practice?
choices: To plan and manage the full lifecycle of all IT assets to maximize value, control costs, manage risks and support decisions about purchase, reuse and retirement
To protect the information needed by the organization to conduct its business
To systematically observe services and service components, and record and report selected changes of state identified as events
To ensure that accurate and reliable information about the configuration of services, and the configuration items that support them, is available when and where needed
questions.explanation: Information security management addresses confidentiality, integrity and availability of information, among other aspects.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the relationship management practice?
choices: To capture demand for incident resolution and service requests, and act as the entry point and single point of contact for the service provider with all its users
To establish and nurture the links between the organization and its stakeholders at strategic and tactical levels
To ensure that the organization's suppliers and their performance are managed appropriately to support the seamless provision of quality products and services
To set clear business-based targets for service levels and ensure delivery of services is properly assessed, monitored and managed against these targets
questions.explanation: Relationship management builds and maintains stakeholder relationships.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the supplier management practice?
choices: To set clear business-based targets for service levels and ensure delivery of services is properly assessed, monitored and managed against these targets
To establish and nurture the links between the organization and its stakeholders at strategic and tactical levels
To ensure that the organization's suppliers and their performance are managed appropriately to support the seamless provision of quality products and services
To plan and manage the full lifecycle of all IT assets to maximize value, control costs, manage risks and support decisions about purchase, reuse and retirement
questions.explanation: Supplier management focuses on managing suppliers and their performance.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the IT asset management practice?
choices: To plan and manage the full lifecycle of all IT assets to maximize value, control costs, manage risks and support decisions about purchase, reuse and retirement
To ensure that the organization's suppliers and their performance are managed appropriately to support the seamless provision of quality products and services
To ensure that accurate and reliable information about the configuration of services, and the configuration items that support them, is available when and where needed
To move new or changed hardware, software, documentation, processes or any other component to live environments
questions.explanation: IT asset management covers assets from acquisition to disposal and supports regulatory and contractual compliance.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the monitoring and event management practice?
choices: To reduce the likelihood and impact of incidents by identifying actual and potential causes of incidents and managing workarounds and known errors
To minimize the negative impact of incidents by restoring normal service operation as quickly as possible
To ensure that accurate and reliable information about the configuration of services, and the configuration items that support them, is available when and where needed
To systematically observe services and service components, and record and report selected changes of state identified as events
questions.explanation: Monitoring and event management detects and records significant changes of state.

questions.prompt: How does ITIL 4 define an event?
choices: A request from a user that initiates a service action agreed as normal
Any change of state that has significance for the management of a service or other configuration item
An unplanned interruption to a service or reduction in the quality of a service
A scheduled modification to a configuration item approved by a change authority
questions.explanation: Events can be informational, warnings or exceptions, and some may lead to incidents.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the release management practice?
choices: To maximize the number of successful service and product changes by ensuring risks are properly assessed, authorizing changes and managing the change schedule
To move new or changed hardware, software, documentation, processes or any other component to live environments
To make new and changed services and features available for use
To protect the information needed by the organization to conduct its business
questions.explanation: Release management controls when new functionality becomes available to users.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the service configuration management practice?
choices: To systematically observe services and service components, and record and report selected changes of state identified as events
To maximize the number of successful service and product changes by ensuring risks are properly assessed, authorizing changes and managing the change schedule
To ensure that accurate and reliable information about the configuration of services, and the configuration items that support them, is available when and where needed
To plan and manage the full lifecycle of all IT assets to maximize value, control costs, manage risks and support decisions about purchase, reuse and retirement
questions.explanation: Service configuration management maintains information about CIs and their relationships.

questions.prompt: How does ITIL 4 define a configuration item (CI)?
choices: Any change of state that has significance for the management of a service
Any component that needs to be managed in order to deliver an IT service
Any user or customer who is registered to consume an IT service
Any financially valuable component that can contribute to delivering an IT product or service
questions.explanation: CIs include hardware, software, documentation and other components whose configuration must be controlled.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the deployment management practice?
choices: To maximize the number of successful service and product changes by ensuring risks are properly assessed, authorizing changes and managing the change schedule
To make new and changed services and features available for use
To move new or changed hardware, software, documentation, processes or any other component to live environments
To ensure that accurate and reliable information about the configuration of services, and the configuration items that support them, is available when and where needed
questions.explanation: Deployment management handles moving components into live (and sometimes other) environments, separate from releasing them to users.

questions.prompt: A new feature is deployed to production but hidden behind a feature flag until the marketing launch, when it is switched on for users. Which practices handle the deployment and the launch respectively?
choices: Deployment management and release management
Change enablement and service request management
Service configuration management and IT asset management
Release management and deployment management
questions.explanation: Deployment moves the component to the live environment; release makes it available for use.

questions.prompt: How does ITIL 4 define an IT asset?
choices: Any document that describes the utility and warranty of a service
Any component that needs to be managed in order to deliver an IT service
Any change of state that has significance for the management of a service
Any financially valuable component that can contribute to the delivery of an IT product or service
questions.explanation: IT assets are defined by financial value; CIs are defined by the need to manage them for service delivery.
